SMH.

Please, take an anatomy class. Your ribs extend out from the spinal column yes, but.... the cracked part of the ribs would have to be in such a place as to be in the posterior portion of the rib cage, which would more indicate a full fracture vs. a crack (if any of the reports are true of course). With that being the case, not only would they have to be fully fractured, but they would have to be in such a place that the fracture happened on the inside curvature of the ribs so the ribs would have to be given an outward force. This goes against the idea that the ribcage would be fractured from a frontal blow but instead would have had to happen from a blow to the back in such a way as to enlarge them. And even then the stress fracture would have to have occurred in the same plane of the kidneys.

I realize not everyone has a degree in a medical field, but cracked ribs occur most frequently in the anterior portion of the ribs, not the posterior. On top of that as I said above, it would have to be 1-1billion of a chance that this exact situation caused the injury.
